chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated from Hamdan al-Qalanisi from Ishaq ibn Bunan from Ibn Baqqah from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) would, if the one who swore (not to have intercourse) refused to divorce, place him in an enclosure of reeds and give him one-fourth of his food until he divorced.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.الْمُؤْلِي: The one who takes an oath of abstinence (ila)

ai.seo_question: How did Imam Ali resolve the issue of a husband refusing both intercourse and divorce?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of 'ibadat (conjugal abstinence) by Imam Ali (AS), who employed a coercive measure of confining the recalcitrant husband in a reed enclosure and reducing his sustenance to one-quarter until he granted divorce. This mechanism highlights the Shia juristic view of the Imam's authority to enforce marital rights when a husband unreasonably withholds intimacy without initiating talaq, ensuring the wife is not left in a state of limbo. The reduction of food serves as a tangible incentive, reflecting the principle of 'darar' (harm) prevention within the marital contract.
